newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: STIC expects 1996 to be better than 1995.
newsitem.headline: STIC expects 1996 to be better than 1995.

text.p: Singapore Technologies Industrial Corp (STIC) said on Tuesday it expects its group results for financial year 1996 to be better than 1995.
At a press briefing for the group's interim results, STIC president Tay Siew Choon said the management was aiming for a 20 percent growth in earnings in the second half.
He said except for the travel and leisure division, all other businesses showed an improvement in the first half.
In the first half, group turnover rose 23.2 percent to Singapore $766.9 million while net profit rose 20.9 percent to S$30.69 million.
Reviewing the results, Tay said main contributions came from the infrastructure and construction sector, which made up 71 percent of its earnings.

He said contribution from retail and leisure businesses was weighed down mainly by losses from startup costs in its hotel in Bintan, Indonesia. The sector, however, still managed to turn in a profit and contributed 15 percent to earnings.
Group joint ventures suffered a 9.6 percent decline in earnings contribution to S$1.99 million.

On the group's two industrial parks in Indonesia, the one in Batam was the most profitable contributing profit of S$6.4 million. The smaller Bintan industrial park suffered losses and was expected to stay in the red over the next two years.
STIC's industrial park in Wuxi, China, sustained a small loss in the first half but should turn in a small profit for the whole year, Tay said.

Goh Song How, executive vice president of STIC said the Batam industrial park was currently 100 percent occupied and STIC was in the last leg of development for the 320-hectare park. The Wuxi park has 80 percent occupancy and the group has started building the second phase of 100 hectares.
